# Erdos.p628 — Erdős problem 628

Reference: https://www.erdosproblems.com/628
Imported from google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (`ErdosProblems/628.lean`, theorem `erdos_628`, AMS 5).

Let $G$ be a graph with chromatic number $k$ containing no $K_k$. If $a,b\geq 2$ and $a+b=k+1$
then must there exist two disjoint subgraphs of $G$ with chromatic numbers $\geq a$ and $\geq b$
respectively?

## Statement
∀ (V : Type*) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ)
    (hG_chrom : G.chromaticNumber = (k : ℕ∞))
    (hG_clique : G.CliqueFree k)
    (a b : ℕ) (ha : a ≥ 2) (hb : b ≥ 2) (hab : a + b = k + 1), ∃ (s : Set V),
      (G.induce s).chromaticNumber ≥ (a : ℕ∞) ∧
      (G.induce sᶜ).chromaticNumber ≥ (b : ℕ∞)

## Strategic notes
Open conjecture — prove-or-refute posture applies to sub-claims,
but the root asserts the conjectured statement itself. No
per-problem hints (benchmark integrity).
